overview: Both are common monosaccharides with the same molecular formula, but they differ in structure and where the carbonyl group sits.
genZNote: Glucose and fructose are the same formula wearing different outfits.

aspects.label: Functional Group
aspects.valueA: An aldehyde sugar (aldose) — carbonyl group at carbon 1.
aspects.valueB: A ketone sugar (ketose) — carbonyl group at carbon 2.

aspects.label: Relative Sweetness
aspects.valueB: The sweetest of all naturally occurring sugars.

aspects.label: Common Source
aspects.valueA: Primary sugar in blood; found in starch and many fruits.
aspects.valueB: Found in fruits and honey; combines with glucose to form sucrose.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Both glucose and fructose share the molecular formula C6H12O6 — they're structural isomers, not different compounds by formula.
overlay.memoryTrick: Glucose = aldehyde (aldose). Fructose = ketone (ketose) and the sweetest natural sugar.
overlay.commonMisconception: Fructose is not automatically 'healthier' than glucose just because it's from fruit — excess fructose is metabolised differently and can strain the liver.
